newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Telstra says in wage talks with unions.
newsitem.headline: Telstra says in wage talks with unions.

text.p: Telstra Corp Ltd said on Wednesday it was in talks with its unions over new wage agreements to replace the existing enterprise agreement which expires on October 4, 1997 after two years operation.
Telstra said it has tabled a number of matters it wants to address in the new agreement. These include:
- changes to current consultative and dispute resolution procedures
- rationalisation of various awards and agreements into a single or "core" award, including changes to hours of duty to allow more flexibility in staffing to meet customer requirements
- introduction of a standard job grading system across Telstra and simplification of job classifications
- rationalisation of work related allowances into a consolidated set of allowances
- removal of current limits on the number or proportion of part time/casual employees in the company.
Telstra, which is owned by the Australian government, said in return for the above changes, Telstra would negotiate a salary increase for all employees which would include two components:
- an across the board salary increase, payable from October 1997 and a cash payment based on company performance for the 1997/98 financial year, payable in September/October 1998.
Telstra said two unions had tabled their positions for the negotiations and the other union's claim would be tabled shortly.

"Extensive talks are now underway and are scheduled until the end of August, with the proposal being that staff vote on a new agreement during September, and that it be subject to ratification in October 1997," Telstra said.
Telstra said negotiations with staff and unions started on July 18 on a new workplace enterprise agreement to apply from the October 5, 1997.
